_about: Teaching text for Module 5 (network pharmacology). Check the science before use with students.

questions.q: Why is a network picture useful for a drug that binds several proteins?
options: It shows every protein the drug touches together with the disease genes, so the overlap and the connections become visible
It proves which protein causes the disease
It replaces the need for experiments
questions.why: A network gathers many targets and many disease genes on one map. It generates hypotheses about where they meet. It proves nothing by itself.

questions.q: Celecoxib is designed to block COX-2. What does polypharmacology mean for it?
options: It may also affect other proteins, which can add benefits or side effects
It can only ever bind COX-2
It works only when combined with other drugs
It means the drug is impure
questions.why: Most drugs bind more than one protein. These extra targets can explain unexpected effects, good or bad.

questions.q: What are 'candidate targets' in this workflow?
options: Genes that appear in both the drug-target list and the disease-gene list
Any gene with a high probability from one tool
The genes with the most publications
Genes listed in only the disease database
questions.why: The overlap of the two lists is the starting set. Both the link to the drug and the link to the disease are needed.

hubs.q: A protein has the highest degree in your network. What is the best way to treat it?
options: As a lead to test: it may be central, or simply well studied, so check betweenness, evidence and then experiments
As the proven main target of the drug
As the first protein to drop because hubs are usually noise
As a sign the network is wrong
hubs.why: Hubs are good leads, but well-studied proteins have more recorded interactions, and a drug effect on a hub is not guaranteed. Combine the measures and test in the lab.

claims.text: The network is a computer-based hypothesis about targets and pathways that must be tested in experiments.
claims.why: This is the honest statement. Predictions, scores and thresholds all carry uncertainty.

claims.text: The network proves how celecoxib works against inflammation.
claims.why: A network cannot prove a mechanism. It was built from predictions and records, and thresholds and background change the result.

claims.text: The hub proteins are the targets of celecoxib.
claims.why: A hub is central in the network. It is not necessarily bound by the drug, and not necessarily a drug target at all.

next.text: Measure whether celecoxib changes the level or activity of the chosen proteins or their pathway in cells (for example by Western blot or ELISA).
Include a positive control: a protein or pathway with known evidence for celecoxib.
Dock celecoxib into the chosen targets and check whether the poses are stable (Modules 1 and 4 logic), keeping in mind that docking also needs checking.
Compare with a second source of data (another database or another prediction tool) and see where they disagree.
Publish the network as proof of mechanism, because the p-values were significant.
Skip experiments, because the hubs were enriched in inflammation pathways.
